idea-plugin.name: CodexCommit
idea-plugin.description: This plugin uses Codex in PyCharm to prepare short commit messages from selected Git changes. Select the files, then select the CodexCommit button. The draft appears in the commit message field. Examine it before you commit. The plugin needs a compatible Codex CLI and an active personal account to work.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Version 1.1.4. Excluded filename warnings name the file and tell you to uncheck it. The installation guide includes Codex setup help and a manual method. Select the button once. The request runs in the background and fills the commit message field. No review windows open. Drafts use a short subject and 1-3 brief bullet points. Select up to 500 tracked files. The combined before and after content can be up to 50 MiB. The plugin detects your saved Codex CLI model or uses the CLI default. The patch can be up to 512 KiB. Whole-file selections work when their editor tabs are closed. Selection errors state the validation failure. The plugin finds native Codex executables. You can also set the executable path. Check selected changes before you use the button. Edit the draft in the commit message field before you commit. The plugin limits file sizes and process time. It stops unsafe selections. You can cancel generation. This release includes source code and local regression tests. Native load and unload passed in an idle IDE. Unload during an active job remains untested.

action.description: Send selected changes to Codex and fill the commit message
